title: an inferred-fallible callback reaching a consumer through a const alias, a double alias or an object property is the same value that reaches it directly, and needs the same Result contract
notes: specification/failures.mdx, 'Inference and Public Contracts': 'Public, abstract, ambient, and declaration-only contracts MUST express fallibility directly with `Result<A, E>` or `Promise<Result<A, E>>`.' A callback boundary is a VALUE edge: the consumer invokes whatever function value it received, and how the author spelled the reference to that value has nothing to do with whether the value can throw. WHY THIS CASE EXISTS: one alias hop defeated this rule. The resolver followed a direct reference to a function declaration and stopped at a `const` binding, so `const alias = fallible; apply("ada", alias)` was accepted — and the failure this rule exists to catch is silent rather than loud. Measured before the fix, the aliased program COMPILED, ran to exit 0, and the throw was swallowed inside the consumer with no diagnostic anywhere. That is a checked failure disappearing, which is the exact loss `SMITHERS1303` prevents. THE DIRECT SPELLING AT LINE 19 IS THE ATTRIBUTION CONTROL: it was already refused, so it is what says the other three rows are the new statement rather than a symptom of this file being rejected wholesale. The three indirect spellings are chosen so that a resolver which learns one does not automatically pass the others: a single `const` hop, TWO hops (so a fix that follows exactly one initializer is caught), and a property of an object literal, which is a different resolution mechanism from a binding entirely. WHAT THIS CASE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PIN: the message. `SMITHERS1303` carries one fixed sentence, byte-identical on both backends, that names the rule and the remediation and no part of this program. It also does not pin a callback aliased through a MUTABLE binding or one returned from a helper — both are recorded open residuals on both backends, and a case for either would need an `xfail` on both sides rather than stating what the language promises. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the declared line 30 to 29 — the double-alias row moved onto its own `const second = first` line, which is where a rule that reported at the last resolution hop rather than at the argument would land — turns the case red on BOTH backends with the position diff printed, and the file was restored byte-identically (sha256 61e62d40f0a47814204dd238f4f5edc5b4c2ef16f33c101a23192da3d883ea07 before and after, that digest being this file's content at the moment the mutation ran — the sentence recording it is appended afterwards, so the shipped file necessarily hashes differently). The paired positive control is `an-aliased-total-callback-needs-no-contract`, the same four spellings over a callback that cannot throw, which must keep compiling AND RUNNING.
